title: HDFC Bank shares cross ₹811 as shareholders approve Bagchi’s appointment - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
HDFC Bank shares rose 1.70 per cent to ₹811.70 on the NSE by 12.30 pm Wednesday, gaining ₹13.55 over Tuesday’s close of ₹798.15, as the stock continued its recovery from the 52-week low of ₹669.20 hit on October 28. The stock opened at ₹810.10, touched an intraday high of ₹817.85, and held above ₹805.70. Total market capitalisation climbed to ₹12,53,960.59 crore. Traded volume stood at 337.09 lakh shares worth ₹2,739.73 crore, with deliverable quantity at 66.97 per cent. The P/E ratio expanded to 15.38, with the adjusted figure at 15.16.

The session coincides with the formal completion of a key governance milestone. Per a regulatory filing dated November 6, 2026, shareholders approved the appointment of Anup Bagchi as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer through a postal ballot, with 98.646 per cent of votes cast in favour. Of the 48,13,947 total members, 12,822 exercised their votes, representing 1,025,73,77,196 shares. No promoter votes were cast, as the promoter and promoter group held no shares.

Institutional sentiment also provided tailwinds. Motilal Oswal named HDFC Bank among its top sector ideas, citing an expected earnings uplift from Q4 as surplus FCNR(B)-driven liquidity gets deployed. Jefferies flagged the bank as a direct beneficiary of returning foreign portfolio investor flows, noting large-cap valuations have turned more reasonable. Bernstein maintained financials as its preferred sector.

Bank Nifty opened sharply higher near 60,525, with the RSI at 78 — in overbought territory — signalling strong momentum but flagging the possibility of intermittent profit-booking. Support lies at 60,000–59,800. The stock’s year-to-date loss has narrowed to 18.04 per cent, against the Nifty 50’s 3.20 per cent decline.
